hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.

hypothesis: LightGBM with a lambdarank (pairwise) objective, training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user, and a within-user-varying feature frame (base5 + dur_feats + item_agg + cross_agg) will beat the pointwise FM baseline by a large margin.
rationale: This attacks the three structural mismatches simultaneously. (a) The loss: the baseline optimises pointwise logloss while the metric is a within-user ordering metric, so gradients currently spend capacity on calibrating absolute probability rather than on the only thing scored, relative order [POINTWISE_BASELINE][WITHIN_USER_RANKING]. (b) The group shape: with group_chunk=6 the training lists (~6 rows, chronologically contiguous) match the ~5.6-row valid lists, so the NDCG position discount and pair sampling see the same list-length regime they will be evaluated in [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]. (c) The features: item_agg (OOF item/author long-view and click rates) and cross_agg (user-author affinity, user-tag affinity, duration relative to the user's historically long-viewed duration) plus dur_feats (within-user duration percentile) all vary across a user's own rows, which is the necessary condition for changing that user's order; the organizers' dead-end feature study only added static fields whose value is largely absorbed by the user x item embedding, and user-side-only terms contribute exactly nothing [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT][ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD]. Trees also handle the continuous rate/affinity features that an embedding FM cannot represent at all. Three seeds so the measurement is not confused with the 0.0008 seed sigma.
expected_gain_derivation: Decomposition of the headroom: baseline 0.6016, perfect 0.8484, so 0.247 of exploitable range [CEILING]. I attribute roughly a third of my expected gain to the loss/group change and two thirds to features that vary within user. Published-style deltas for pointwise->pairwise on ~6-item lists are typically +0.01 to +0.02 on a GAUC/nDCG blend [POINTWISE_BASELINE][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; OOF item-quality rates plus duration contrast are usually worth another +0.02 to +0.04 on KuaiRand-like logs because item long-view propensity is the dominant reorderable signal and it varies within user [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]. Summing conservatively and discounting for the possibility that user x video embeddings already absorbed much of it [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] gives ~+0.045, i.e. a primary near 0.646.

hypothesis: LightGBM lambdarank on a purely generalising, within-user-varying frame (dur_feats + item_agg + cross_agg, with base5 IDs REMOVED) and stronger leaf regularisation will beat both the FM baseline and iteration 1 by ~0.03.
rationale: Iteration 1 had the ranking loss, the matched group size and the good features, yet landed exactly on the baseline (0.60163). The one component it shared with the baseline was the high-cardinality ID block: user_id/video_id/author_id as LightGBM categoricals with max_cat_threshold=64 let trees memorise ID partitions over a 43-rows/user train window, and those splits dominate gain while generalising poorly into a thinned, regime-shifted valid log [EXPOSURE_REGIME_CHANGE]. user_id is user-constant so it can contribute nothing to within-user order anyway [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT], and video_id memorisation is exactly the kind of exposure-correlated signal that the CF observation says behaves badly on the standard log [CF_DIAGNOSTIC_DIVERGENCE]. Dropping the IDs forces the model onto duration-relative-to-user, item OOF long-view rate and user x author/tag affinity, all of which vary within a user list and all of which transfer across the regime break.
expected_gain_derivation: Ceiling is 0.8484 with only 57.8% of users influenceable [CEILING], so headroom above 0.6016 is ~0.25 of primary. Duration-conditioned and item-quality features are the known dominant signal for long_view and vary within list [WITHIN_USER_RANKING][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; typical GBDT gains on such frames are 0.03-0.06 primary. I discount to +0.030 because iteration 1 already contained these blocks and returned 0.000, so the whole gain must come from removing ID memorisation, which is a hypothesis not yet tested.

hypothesis: Keep the model family that actually fits this data (the factorization machine, whose user_id x video_id interaction the organizers say absorbs most of the signal) but swap its pointwise logloss for the pairwise lambdarank loss with training groups chunked to 6 rows per user, i.e. the organizers' #1 unexplored direction applied to the only model that has ever reached 0.60 here.
rationale: Iteration 2 showed that dropping the ID fields costs 0.016, so the memorised user/item interaction is the load-bearing signal; iteration 1 showed that a tree model cannot beat FM even with rich engineered features, because 26k x 7k ID interactions are not representable by axis-aligned splits. So the productive move is not more features or another tree variant, it is changing the objective on the factorized model. Pointwise logloss spends capacity on calibrating P(long_view) globally, including the large user-level offset which is provably irrelevant [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]; a pairwise loss over within-user groups puts all gradient on within-user contrasts, exactly the quantity the metric scores [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]. Chunking to 6 aligns the training list length and position discount with the ~6-item evaluation lists [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]. This is the highest-variance move available in the spec: it either errors (loss may be wired only to lightgbm) or it moves the metric a lot.
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]: under logloss a large fraction of the FM's fitted variance is the user first-order/user-embedding-magnitude term that cannot reorder anything, so removing it from the loss frees capacity for within-user contrasts. Published pointwise->pairwise swaps on within-list ranking typically move NDCG on short lists by 0.02-0.05 relative; here only 57.8% of users are influenceable [CEILING], so the realisable move is scaled by ~0.58, giving ~+0.015-0.03 if it works. I discount by ~35% for the chance the harness rejects lambdarank for model=fm or the FM pairwise implementation is weak, giving 0.018.

designation_reason: best-valid config from iteration 1 (primary 0.60163); hypothesis: 'LightGBM with a lambdarank (pairwise) objective, training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user, and a within-user-varying feature frame (base5 + dur_feats + item_agg + cross_agg) will beat the pointwise FM baseline by a large margin.'. Divergence between best-valid and structurally-justified, if any, is resolved per POLICY.md section 6 at designation review.
convergence_reason: validation primary did not improve by more than 0.002 over 3 consecutive iterations
